question: An article is bought for Rs. 5,000 and sold for Rs. 6,200. Find the profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 5000 : 6200 = 25 : 31

Profit in ratio = 31 − 25 = 6 units

Profit % = (6 ÷ 25) × 100 = 24%

**∴ The correct answer is 24%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 5,000

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 6,200

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP = ₹5,000
 
 
 ₹1,200

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 SP = ₹6,200

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = 6200 − 5000

⇒ Profit = 1200

⇒ Profit % = (1200 ÷ 5000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (12 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 12 × 2 = 24%

**∴ The correct answer is 24%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Selling Price is less than Cost Price, Loss is incurred. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the effective discount % is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.
